memories.content: Link each HCI research question directly to corresponding user data and analysis procedures.
In preregistered studies, specify the conditions under which deviations from the plan are permissible.
In preregistered studies, specify how to record content that deviates from the plan.
Commit to one exact target number of participants so the schedule, workload, and budget can be checked against the same quantity.
Specify the interview protocols, recording devices, or log tools used to collect each type of user data.
Specify whether each type of user data is collected before, during, or after the interaction.
Readers cannot tell whether the schedule and budget agree when different sections imply different target counts.
In formative evaluation prototypes, implementation instability exists as an independent cause of task failure alongside design choices.
If a prototype safety signal occurs during formative evaluation, existing institutional safety procedures take precedence over planned data collection.
Reviewers judge answerability by tracing the path from each research question to the data and analysis.
The author of this proposal tends to present implemented feature lists directly as design contributions.
Calculate the required sessions, facilitator hours, and participant payments from the same exact target rather than from separate rough estimates.
If recruitment falls below the exact target, state the shortfall explicitly and revise the affected schedule or deliverable.
Do not use a wide range merely to postpone choosing the quantity that the rest of the proposal must support.
Link anticipated participant burden with its mitigation strategies for each field user study task.
Specify the accommodations necessary for participants to access the field system and research tasks.
Specify how accessibility accommodations will be provided in the field user study.
Describe how personal identifiers will be separated from research data immediately upon collection.
List equipment to be loaned when participants lack necessary gear.
Describe the procedure for returning equipment loaned to participants.
The HCI ethics reviewer verifies that anticipated burden and mitigation strategies correspond for each field user study task.
Ensure that participants can safely return to existing work procedures if they discontinue research participation.
Specify that organizational members who decline research participation will not face disadvantages in task assignment or performance evaluation.
The user's withdrawal risk can be adequately assessed only when a safe alternative procedure exists for field tasks.
The user tends to assume that a short session also entails little burden from work interruption and exposure to a manager.

analysis.overview: The reference frame concentrates on research traceability, preregistration, participant-count consistency, data-collection specification, prototype evaluation, and proposal framing. The compared frame independently addresses field-study burden, accessibility, privacy, equipment, withdrawal, nonparticipation, and a burden-related assumption. No claims govern the same operational decision closely enough for a cross-frame relation.

relations.reason: The reference memories state the same one-sided traceability requirement from authoring and reviewer perspectives; the compared frame contains no corresponding claim.
relations.summary: Research questions should be directly traceable to their supporting user data and analysis procedures so reviewers can assess answerability.

relations.reason: These reference memories split one governance requirement for preregistration deviations into permission conditions and documentation; the compared frame contains no corresponding policy.
relations.summary: Preregistered studies should define both when plan deviations are permitted and how deviating content is recorded.

relations.reason: These reference memories state and motivate one participant-planning consistency claim; the compared frame contains no corresponding quantity-planning requirement.
relations.summary: A proposal should use one exact participant target consistently across scheduling, workload, budgeting, sessions, facilitator hours, and payments rather than defer commitment with a wide range.

relations.reason: This collection-instrument specification appears only in the reference frame and is independently useful.
relations.summary: Each type of user data should identify the interview protocol, recording device, or logging tool used to collect it.

relations.reason: This temporal collection specification appears only in the reference frame and is distinct from identifying collection instruments.
relations.summary: Each type of user data should specify whether collection occurs before, during, or after interaction.

relations.reason: This causal interpretation of prototype failure appears only in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Formative evaluation should recognize implementation instability as a cause of task failure independent of design choices.

relations.reason: This safety-signal escalation rule appears only in the reference frame; compared-frame withdrawal safeguards address a different operational decision.
relations.summary: During formative evaluation, an observed prototype safety signal should make existing institutional safety procedures take precedence over planned data collection.

relations.reason: This author-specific proposal-framing tendency appears only in the reference frame.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to present implemented feature lists directly as design contributions.

relations.reason: This contingency for an unmet recruitment target appears only in the reference frame and is distinct from initially choosing a consistent target.
relations.summary: If recruitment misses the exact target, the shortfall should be disclosed and affected schedules or deliverables revised.

relations.reason: The compared memories state the same one-sided task-level burden-and-mitigation requirement from authoring and reviewer perspectives; the reference frame contains no corresponding claim.
relations.summary: For every field-study task, anticipated participant burden should be linked to corresponding mitigation strategies so ethics reviewers can verify the match.

relations.reason: These compared memories split one accessibility-accommodation requirement into identification and provision; the reference frame contains no corresponding claim.
relations.summary: A field user study should specify both the accommodations participants need to access the system and tasks and how those accommodations will be provided.

relations.reason: This privacy-handling requirement appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Personal identifiers should be separated from research data immediately upon collection through a described procedure.

relations.reason: This equipment-access requirement appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: A field study should list equipment loaned to participants who lack necessary gear.

relations.reason: This equipment-return procedure appears only in the compared frame and is operationally independent from listing equipment to be loaned.
relations.summary: A field study should describe how participants return loaned equipment.

relations.reason: These compared memories state the same underlying safe-withdrawal requirement as a safeguard and an assessment rationale; the reference frame contains no corresponding field-task withdrawal claim.
relations.summary: Withdrawal risk in field tasks should be assessed against a safe alternative procedure that lets participants return to existing work practices after discontinuing participation.

relations.reason: This protection against workplace consequences for nonparticipation appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Organizational members who decline participation should face no disadvantage in task assignments or performance evaluations.

relations.reason: This user-specific assumption about field-study burden appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: The user tends to infer from a short session that work interruption and exposure to a manager impose little burden.

reports.compared_only: Compared-only material covers task burden, accommodations, identifier separation, equipment loans and returns, safe withdrawal, protection for nonparticipants, and assumptions about interruption and managerial exposure.
reports.reference_only: Reference-only material covers research-question traceability, preregistration deviations, exact participant planning, collection methods and timing, prototype failure and safety, recruitment shortfalls, and proposal framing.
